title: Opus Clip Pricing 2026: Free, Starter and Pro Plans
summary: Opus Clip pricing includes three tiers with different features and costs. Compare what each plan offers to find the option that fits your needs.
body_markdown:
## Automate the hand-off after Opus Clip with Activepieces


Without anyone dragging files around, Activepieces can carry finished clips from Opus Clip to review, storage and scheduling. It bills 1 credit per flow run, so a ten-step hand-off costs the same as a two-step one.


The run is the meter, not the steps inside it, which is the reverse of Zapier's per-task billing. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


Splitting export, backup, review and scheduling into small steps adds nothing, and the Opus Clip plan stays fixed by the minutes you feed in.


That distinction matters for the math. Every clip you move by hand costs a few minutes of attention, and that cost recurs on every batch. Automating it shrinks the labor line, not the subscription line.


If your volume pushed you toward a higher tier, Activepieces won't talk you back down: at 1 credit a run, its free plan's 1,000 credits a month cover 1,000 hand-offs, with unlimited flows.


If your volume fits a cheaper tier, it won't make that tier cheaper either.


### What can be automated and what cannot


After export, Activepieces handles the mechanical steps.


These are noticing that new files have landed in a folder, copying them to cloud storage, notifying a reviewer, and queuing approved clips in a scheduler, across its 747 integrations, counted from an open source monorepo whose core is MIT-licensed.


The steps are repeatable, rule-based moves, which is exactly where a workflow tool earns its keep.


It can't do the work Opus Clip charges for. Clipping, captioning, and removing the watermark all happen inside Opus Clip, so none of them moves to a different tool or a cheaper plan through a workflow.


Nor can Activepieces judge whether a clip is any good.


In OpenKrill's test only 11 of 27 clips went out as they were, so a person still has to make that call, and the workflow's job is to put the clip in front of them quickly, not to replace them.


### A simple clip-review workflow


Left to right, the flow starts at the folder where you export from Opus Clip and ends in three places.


In the illustration, the export folder feeds one Activepieces node, which fans out to a review notification, cloud storage and a scheduler.


Its note, "Opus Clip plan unchanged," is the point to take away. Everything to the right of the folder is downstream of what you already pay for.


In practice, the steps run in this order:


1. A new file appears in the export folder.
2. Activepieces copies it to cloud storage so a backup exists before anyone touches it.
3. A notification goes to the reviewer with a link to the clip.
4. Once the reviewer approves it, the clip is added to the scheduler.


Build it once and each batch of exports costs you the review itself, nothing more. Next comes the choice of plan, with the workflow already in place.


Activepieces is the better fit for anyone automating the hand-off after Opus Clip, such as export, backup, review and scheduling, when the criterion is how the bill scales with workflow complexity.


It charges 1 credit per flow run, so a ten-step hand-off costs the same as a two-step one, while Zapier bills per task and Make per module, as each publishes on its pricing page.


Teams whose hand-offs stay short may see little difference between the three, but for those who want to split the work into many small steps without watching the meter, Activepieces is the better fit.
